results.name: single_example_cell_polarization
results.description: Among (set, target) cells from one-example sets, fraction of cells whose yes-rate is <=1/9 or >=8/9; observed > null means people answer all-or-none after a lone example even though the model (no coincidence, so its least-steep slope) predicts graded answers there; observed < null means the model is too polarized there.

results.name: incoherent_multi_cell_polarization
results.description: Among (set, target) cells from 2-4-example sets with no coincidence (examples differ in parity, are not all multiples of 5, and do not share a final digit), fraction of cells with yes-rate <=1/9 or >=8/9; observed > null means people are all-or-none even after incoherent multi-example sets (decisiveness not confined to coherent sets), observed < null means the model over-polarizes them.
results.code:
# name: incoherent_multi_cell_polarization
# description: Among (set, target) cells from 2-4-example sets with no coincidence (examples differ in parity, are not all multiples of 5, and do not share a final digit), fraction of cells with yes-rate <=1/9 or >=8/9; observed > null means people are all-or-none even after incoherent multi-example sets (decisiveness not confined to coherent sets), observed < null means the model over-polarizes them.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric)
    n = s.notna().sum(axis=1)
    par = s % 2
    same_par = par.max(axis=1) == par.min(axis=1)
    dig = s % 10
    same_dig = dig.max(axis=1) == dig.min(axis=1)
    f5 = ((s % 5 == 0) | s.isna()).all(axis=1)
    inc = (n >= 2) & ~same_par & ~same_dig & ~f5
    d = df[inc.values]
    y = d.groupby(["number_set", "target"])["rating"].mean()
    if len(y) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(((y <= 1/9 + 1e-9) | (y >= 8/9 - 1e-9)).mean())

results.name: within_item_trial_drift
results.description: Correlation between trial_index and the rating after subtracting each (set, target) cell's mean rating; observed > null means people become more liberal (more yes) later in the session, observed < null more conservative/fatigued, a time trend the stationary model cannot produce.

results.name: digit_rule_violation_proximity_contrast
results.description: In 2-4-example sets whose examples all share a final digit, yes-rate for wrong-final-digit targets within 10 of some example minus that for wrong-digit targets more than 20 from every example; observed < null means people reject digit-rule violators flatly regardless of distance while the model still lets near violators ride on magnitude similarity (observed > null: people's violation rejection is more distance-graded than the model's).
results.code:
# name: digit_rule_violation_proximity_contrast
# description: In 2-4-example sets whose examples all share a final digit, yes-rate for wrong-final-digit targets within 10 of some example minus that for wrong-digit targets more than 20 from every example; observed < null means people reject digit-rule violators flatly regardless of distance while the model still lets near violators ride on magnitude similarity (observed > null: people's violation rejection is more distance-graded than the model's).
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric)
    n = s.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    dig = s % 10
    same_dig = (dig.max(axis=1) == dig.min(axis=1)).to_numpy() & (n >= 2)
    viol = same_dig & (t % 10 != dig[0].to_numpy())
    mind = np.nanmin(np.abs(s.to_numpy(dtype=float) - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a = viol & (mind <= 10)
    b = viol & (mind > 20)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: partial_digit_majority_contrast
results.description: In 3-4-example sets where all but exactly one example share a final digit, yes-rate for targets ending in that majority digit minus yes-rate for targets whose final digit matches no example; observed > null means people treat a near-unanimous digit as a rule (a near-coincidence the model ignores, since its rule/violation term needs all examples to agree), observed < null means the model over-credits the majority digit.
results.code:
# name: partial_digit_majority_contrast
# description: In 3-4-example sets where all but exactly one example share a final digit, yes-rate for targets ending in that majority digit minus yes-rate for targets whose final digit matches no example; observed > null means people treat a near-unanimous digit as a rule (a near-coincidence the model ignores, since its rule/violation term needs all examples to agree), observed < null means the model over-credits the majority digit.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric)
    S = s.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    valid = ~np.isnan(S)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    D = np.where(valid, np.where(valid, S, 0) % 10, -1)
    counts = np.stack([(D == d).sum(axis=1) for d in range(10)], axis=1)
    maj = counts.argmax(axis=1)
    mc = counts.max(axis=1)
    part = (n >= 3) & (mc == n - 1)
    td = t % 10
    match_maj = td == maj
    match_any = (D == td[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a = part & match_maj
    b = part & ~match_any
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: parity_vs_digit_rule_violation_gap
results.description: Yes-rate for wrong-parity targets in 2-4-example same-parity sets that do not share a final digit and are not all multiples of 5, minus yes-rate for wrong-final-digit targets in same-final-digit sets; observed > null means people tolerate breaking a weak parity rule more (and/or a digit rule less) than the model's single shared violation cost implies, observed < null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: parity_vs_digit_rule_violation_gap
# description: Yes-rate for wrong-parity targets in 2-4-example same-parity sets that do not share a final digit and are not all multiples of 5, minus yes-rate for wrong-final-digit targets in same-final-digit sets; observed > null means people tolerate breaking a weak parity rule more (and/or a digit rule less) than the model's single shared violation cost implies, observed < null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric)
    n = s.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    e0 = s[0].to_numpy().astype(int)
    dig = s % 10
    same_dig = (dig.max(axis=1) == dig.min(axis=1)).to_numpy() & (n >= 2)
    f5 = ((s % 5 == 0) | s.isna()).all(axis=1).to_numpy()
    par = s % 2
    same_par = (par.max(axis=1) == par.min(axis=1)).to_numpy() & (n >= 2)
    pset = same_par & ~same_dig & ~f5
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a = pset & (t % 2 != e0 % 2)
    b = same_dig & (t % 10 != e0 % 10)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: violation_rate_set_size_contrast
results.description: Yes-rate for coincidence-rule-breaking targets (wrong final digit / not multiple of 5 / wrong parity, by the set's most specific shared coincidence) in 4-example coherent sets minus the same in 2-example coherent sets; observed > null (less negative) means rejection of rule-breakers barely strengthens with more examples while the model's coincidence-scaled slope drives 4-example violators much closer to zero, observed < null means people strengthen it more than the model.
results.code:
# name: violation_rate_set_size_contrast
# description: Yes-rate for coincidence-rule-breaking targets (wrong final digit / not multiple of 5 / wrong parity, by the set's most specific shared coincidence) in 4-example coherent sets minus the same in 2-example coherent sets; observed > null (less negative) means rejection of rule-breakers barely strengthens with more examples while the model's coincidence-scaled slope drives 4-example violators much closer to zero, observed < null means people strengthen it more than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric)
    n = s.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    e0 = s[0].to_numpy().astype(int)
    dig = s % 10
    same_dig = (dig.max(axis=1) == dig.min(axis=1)).to_numpy()
    f5 = ((s % 5 == 0) | s.isna()).all(axis=1).to_numpy()
    par = s % 2
    same_par = (par.max(axis=1) == par.min(axis=1)).to_numpy()
    viol = np.where(same_dig, t % 10 != e0 % 10,
           np.where(f5, t % 5 != 0, np.where(same_par, t % 2 != e0 % 2, False))) & (n >= 2)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a = viol & (n == 4)
    b = viol & (n == 2)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: coherent_violator_arithmetic_contrast
results.description: Among targets that break the coincidence rule of a 2-4-example coherent set (wrong final digit for same-digit sets, else not a multiple of 5 for all-multiple-of-5 sets, else wrong parity for same-parity sets), yes-rate for targets that are a multiple (>1, not equal) or factor-kin (gcd>=3, neither divides the other) of some example minus yes-rate for violators with neither relation; observed > null means arithmetic kinship rescues rule-breakers more than the model's uniform share-of-support cut allows, observed < null means it rescues them less.
results.code:
# name: coherent_violator_arithmetic_contrast
# description: Among targets that break the coincidence rule of a 2-4-example coherent set (wrong final digit for same-digit sets, else not a multiple of 5 for all-multiple-of-5 sets, else wrong parity for same-parity sets), yes-rate for targets that are a multiple (>1, not equal) or factor-kin (gcd>=3, neither divides the other) of some example minus yes-rate for violators with neither relation; observed > null means arithmetic kinship rescues rule-breakers more than the model's uniform share-of-support cut allows, observed < null means it rescues them less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric)
    S = s.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = s.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    T = t[:, None].astype(float)
    dig = s % 10
    same_dig = (dig.max(axis=1) == dig.min(axis=1)).to_numpy()
    f5 = ((s % 5 == 0) | s.isna()).all(axis=1).to_numpy()
    par = s % 2
    same_par = (par.max(axis=1) == par.min(axis=1)).to_numpy()
    e0 = S[:, 0].astype(int)
    viol = np.where(same_dig, t % 10 != e0 % 10,
           np.where(f5, t % 5 != 0, np.where(same_par, t % 2 != e0 % 2, False))) & (n >= 2)
    valid = ~np.isnan(S)
    Si = np.where(valid, S, 1).astype(int)
    Ti = np.broadcast_to(t[:, None], Si.shape)
    mult = valid & (Si > 1) & (Ti % Si == 0) & (Ti != Si)
    g = np.gcd(Ti, Si)
    fk = valid & (g >= 3) & (Ti % Si != 0) & (Si % Ti != 0)
    rel = (mult | fk).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a = viol & rel
    b = viol & ~rel
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
